summary: Build practical skills for modern slavery risk assessment, remediation, and reporting. Explore the five-day human rights due diligence course.
lede: Human rights due diligence helps procurement, sustainability, compliance and audit teams identify and address modern slavery risks across supply chains. Participants practise mapping supplier relationships, assessing recruitment and worker vulnerability risks, and prioritizing findings in a risk register. They also develop grievance and remediation plans and use supplier data to support monitoring and evidence-based reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who translate human rights commitments into procurement controls, supplier engagement, workplace safeguards, remediation, and executive reporting. It suits intermediate practitioners with some exposure to supply chain, compliance, sustainability, audit, or labour standards processes.

prerequisites: You should have working exposure to procurement, supply chain management, sustainability, compliance, audit, labour standards, or responsible sourcing. No legal qualification or programming experience is required. Familiarity with supplier records, risk assessments, or corrective action processes will help you apply the exercises. Advanced topics such as AI-assisted screening and reporting assurance are taught at operational application level, not technical engineering level.
